walkthroughs.body_html:
Internal Assessment: Historical Investigation — a core area of History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Internal Assessment: Historical Investigation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Internal Assessment: Historical Investigation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which Bolshevik slogan summarised Lenin's April Theses?
options: Peace, Land, Bread
Workers of the world unite
Liberte, egalite, fraternite
Better dead than red

mcqs.q: What was the immediate cause of the February Revolution?
options: German invasion
Bread shortages in Petrograd
Lenin's return from Switzerland
Kerensky's offensive

mcqs.q: Why did Stalin force collectivisation from 1929?
options: The killings only began after Germany lost the Battle of Stalingrad.
Collectivisation was popular with peasants who wanted to share land.
To fund industrialisation by extracting grain, eliminate independent kulak farmers as a political threat, and impose Communist control on the countryside.
Collectivisation was suggested by Trotsky and Stalin opposed it.

mcqs.q: When did the systematic mass murder of Jews begin?
options: Mass shootings by Einsatzgruppen began with Operation Barbarossa in June 1941; industrial extermination camps followed from 1942.
The Holocaust began as soon as Hitler came to power in 1933.
The killings only began after Germany lost the Battle of Stalingrad.
William was Edward the Confessor's eldest son.
